verdict.rationale: Daytona's docs say it can capture and persist a sandbox's current state. VM sandboxes get hot snapshots of both filesystem and memory, but container sandboxes get filesystem-only cold snapshots, so memory preservation depends on sandbox type. The evidence never describes an explicit pause/resume workflow, only snapshot capture and CLI lifecycle management. Missing for 10: an explicit pause/resume operation with documented restore of a running sandbox, memory-state retention for container sandboxes, and independent or hands-on corroboration that resumed sandboxes keep their memory state.

support.subject: As a developer, I can pause a running sandbox and resume it later with filesystem and memory state intact

citations.quote: captures and persists a sandbox’s current state; container sandboxes capture filesystem state only (cold snapshots), VM sandboxes capture filesystem and memory state (hot snapshots)
Snapshots are persistent, point-in-time captures of sandbox state, including the filesystem, installed packages, dependencies, and settings.
